target.title: fix: respect local Crabbox provider preferences
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where OpenClaw agents could ignore a developer's configured Crabbox provider and force Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. The repository wrapper also selected provider-specific behavior from only `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` and `.crabbox.yaml`, which could disagree with Crabbox's effective user configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The wrapper now resolves the same effective provider reported by `crabbox config show --json`, while preserving explicit command-line overrides, `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`, platform constraints, and untrusted-source safety routing. Provider resolution fails closed when effective configuration cannot be read, preventing wrapper and CLI behavior from diverging.

The testing and Crabbox skills now use the effective backend for ordinary trusted work. They explicitly distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and require provider attribution from wrapper/config output instead of inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

AI-assisted: this change was implemented, agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, and reviewed with Codex. The author understands the provider precedence, isolation, and fail-closed behavior introduced here.

## User Impact

Developers can choose `local-container`, `aws`, or another eligible provider through their normal Crabbox configuration without editing the shared OpenClaw skill. Developers without a local preference continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default. A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution.

## Evidence

- Blind agent validation through `acpx claude`:
  - Claude independently read the repository skills and resolved `crabbox config show --json` to `provider=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
  - The first validation exposed a real guidance defect: Claude ran `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the host after discovering the local provider. That result was rejected as invalid, and the conflicting remote-only/local-fallback skill text was corrected in `45457f9d3ad`.
  - Fresh post-fix Claude runs correctly used the wrapper, provisioned Docker leases, ran the focused test inside the container, and cleaned up their leases.
- Final post-review Docker proof:
  - Provider/runtime: `provider=local-container`, `runtime=docker`, Crabbox `0.37.1`.
  - Lease: `cbx_58c1ad7c78c0` / `coral-krill-93d6`, Ubuntu 26.04 container, then explicitly deleted.
  - Command: `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --id cbx_58c1ad7c78c0 --timing-json --shell -- "pnpm test test/scripts/crabbox-wrapper.test.ts --reporter=default"`.
  - Result: 1 test file passed; 191/191 tests passed.
  - Both new regression cases were also rerun by name inside the same lease; each passed with 190 unrelated cases skipped.
- Earlier independent Docker proof: lease `cbx_64ed1edb7be8` / `amber-shrimp`; 191/191 focused tests passed and the lease was deleted.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --stream-engine-output` — final fresh review clean, no accepted/actionable findings. The prior review's two provider/isolation findings were fixed before this clean run.
